label: model_selection_iter3
prompt:
You are the Model Selection judge. The plan below has already been decided; your one
job is to commit to a concrete model identifier and its hyperparameters.

## Plan

{
  "strategy": "Swap the ranking generator to a structurally different family: an RBF-kernel SVC on standardised, median-imputed columns. This is the first non-tree, non-boosting, non-linear ranking on this dataset — a smooth distance-based decision surface instead of axis-aligned splits, which is the only untested source of a higher ranking (the bar needs KS ~0.934 against the best measured 0.8766, and cut_headroom on both GBDT attempts was 0.008–0.017, so the shortfall is in the ranking, not the cut). Concretely: svc with kernel='rbf', C=10.0, gamma='scale', class_weight left at default (imbalance ratio 1.54 is mild and both GBDT attempts showed only a mildly conservative cut, recall 0.909 vs specificity 0.952, so the operating-point lever is worth at most a fraction of the gap and would confound the family read). Preprocessing: impute median (a no-op — no missing values), scale=true, which the kernel requires because the 57 columns span sub-unit word frequencies and tens-magnitude capital-run counts. 2,760 training rows makes a quadratic-in-rows kernel fit cheap (well inside the 600 s / 2 GB budget). Then read roc_auc, pr_auc and balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut against hist_gbdt's 0.9789 / 0.9577 / 0.9383: if the kernel ranking clears those, iterations 4–5 refine C<path> around this point; if it lands at or below them, three structurally distinct ranking generators will have agreed and the remaining attempts go to the largest available operating-point move (class_weight) on the best ranking, since nothing else on the ranking axis remains.",
  "model_family": "kernel",
  "candidate_models": [
    "svc"
  ],
  "hyperparams": {
    "kernel": "rbf",
    "C": 10.0
  },
  "preprocessing": {
    "impute": "median",
    "scale": true,
    "missing_indicator": false,
    "missing_count": false
  },
  "changes_from_last": "Family changes from gbdt (xgboost, iteration 2; hist_gbdt, iteration 1) to kernel — svc with an RBF kernel, C=10.0, gamma='scale'. Preprocessing changes from scale=false to scale=true, which is mandatory for a distance-based kernel and was never used in either previous attempt. All boosting hyperparameters (n_estimators, learning_rate, max_depth, subsample, colsample_bytree, reg_lambda<path>, min_child_weight) are gone; no class_weight is set, so the operating point is held fixed exactly as in both previous attempts, isolating the ranking change as the single variable.",
  "rationale": "The Critic twice diagnosed wrong_model_family, and the second diagnosis carries the decisive measurement: the two GBDT variants' ranking ceilings (balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut) agree to 0.0002 (0.9383 vs 0.9381) while the bar sits 0.0287 above the better of them. cut_headroom of 0.0081 (it. 1) and 0.0171 (it. 2) bounds what any operating-point lever can buy at well under half the shortfall, so class_weight or another point in GBDT hyperparameter space cannot reach 0.967 — the ranking itself has to improve, which means a different kind of ranking. Capacity is also not the issue: train_balanced_accuracy 0.9991 / 0.9887 with train_val_gap ~0.068 shows both ensembles already fit the 2,760 training rows nearly perfectly, so more trees or depth is spent budget. The untried structural axis is a non-axis-aligned decision surface. Spambase's spam signal lies in the joint magnitude of many co-occurring skewed frequency columns; an RBF kernel on standardised inputs scores rows by smooth distance in that 57-dimensional space rather than by rectangular partitions, and it is a documented strong performer on this benchmark, so it is a genuinely different ranking generator rather than a re-parameterisation of the same one. C=10.0 gives a fairly flexible margin (the boundary is clearly non-linear — the linear baseline's KS was 0.8466) while gamma='scale' keeps the kernel width tied to feature variance after standardisation, avoiding the near-nearest-neighbour degeneracy that large gamma causes with 57 dimensions and only 2,760 training rows. Cost is trivial at this row count. Holding preprocessing (median impute, a no-op here) and the operating point fixed means the resulting roc_auc / balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut is directly comparable to 0.9789 / 0.9383 and gives the remaining two iterations a clean read on whether the ranking axis has any headroom left at all.",
  "unsupported_claims": [],
  "source": "llm",
  "iteration": 3
}
